brief: GS flags a sharp breadth divergence: SPX sits within 1% of all-time highs while the median S&P stock is 16% below its own high, and GS's preferred breadth measure is at its weakest since the Dot-Com Bubble. The GS Quality factor has rallied over 16% in 8 weeks, a flight-to-quality move not seen since COVID, pointing to risk aversion beneath a steady headline index. GS does not read the narrowness as bearish: a Bloomberg study of 13 similar concentration episodes since 1995 shows median SPX gains of +10.1%/+19.6% over six/twelve months, above historical norms, so GS continues to favor SPX higher over the next 1-3 months, helped by light positioning (Sentiment Indicator at -1.3, L/S net leverage in low percentiles, though gross exposure stays elevated). GS's own Prime data shows fundamental L/S funds lost 70bps last week on negative alpha on both longs and shorts, with Tech flows reversing sharply to net-sold after months of buying, while Industrials, Financials and Software saw fresh buying and Staples/Biotech kept de-grossing. Oil and rates are the stated risks to the bullish call, and GS flags cheap NVDA downside vol as a hedge against an AI-trade unwind.
